bull.b: Revenue reached $149M in 2025 with an approximately 38% gross margin, marking a material shift from the company’s earlier no-revenue period. This early commercial traction indicates the product can generate meaningful sales and provides a base from which production scale could support future operating leverage.

EPA certification confirms the Launch Edition meets federal emissions requirements and removes a major regulatory barrier to U.S. sales. This milestone materially advances commercialization, strengthens the credibility of Aptera’s vehicle program, and supports the transition from development toward customer deliveries.

The Shanghai Launch partnership gives Aptera access to manufacturing capabilities and an international supplier network while supporting tooling, testing, pilot builds, and full-scale production. This could improve production readiness, materials economics, and execution capacity as the company targets initial vehicles.

bear.b: Despite higher revenue and gross margin, Aptera remains unprofitable at the operating level, with negative EBITDA and continuing reported losses. Persistent operating losses reduce internally generated funding, increase dependence on external capital, and make the durability of earnings power uncertain during the production ramp.

Negative equity combined with sizable debt leaves Aptera with limited balance-sheet flexibility and a weak capital base. High leverage can constrain investment choices, increase financial pressure during commercialization, and make the company more reliant on successful execution or additional financing to sustain operations.

The cash-flow profile does not yet demonstrate self-funding operations, as prior periods included negative operating and free cash flow and 2025 reported zero for both measures. This limits financial resilience and raises the importance of outside funding while Aptera builds production and delivery volumes.
